newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-ITT says revamp was long-planned.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-ITT says revamp was long-planned.

text.p: ITT Corp Chairman Rand Araskog said Wednesday the company's massive restructuring had been in the works for more than a year and was not motivated by a $6.5 billion hostile bid from rival Hilton Hotels Corp.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, Araskog also shrugged off Hilton's condemnation of the plan and its intention to fight the plan in court.
"What Hilton does, Hilton does. They've got a business to run. They've got a thing to do. We've got a business to run. We've got a thing to do. They can go do whatever they want to do," said Araskog.
In a move widely seen as part of its attempt to thwart Hilton's bid, ITT earlier announced plans to split into three companies and buy back $2.1 billion in stock.
"I can't say they were significant to this comprehensive plan at all. This was really driven by our ability to get all our ducks in a row on what we wanted to do," Araskog said.

"We were implementing this plan with or without Hilton. This is a shareholder enhancement plan that's going to move forward whether Hilton is there or Hilton is not there," added President Robert Bowman.
Araskog said the restructuring was prompted, in part, by a recent rise in the valuation of the highly profitable world telephone directories busines.
"The business has really established its competitive position. We started thinking about this last year," he said.
Hilton launched its bid in January.
However, Araskog admitted that Hilton did play a role in ITT's recent sale of stakes in Madison Square Garden and the WBIS television station.
"We realized we had some extremely valuable assets there that were not giving us earnings per share contribution related to it," he said.
Araskog denied that the proposed staggered board for the newly-planned casino and hotel company called ITT Destinations Inc was a move to thwart a potential Hilton takeover.
"All of our major competitors have it. This is something we should have done before and it is an appropriate thing for us to do now," he said.
